prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation supplies approved-limit transformer/feeder circuits; observation never replaces protection/control/field verification. Bay Automation Controller (Juniper): North Bay Controller/South Bay Controller have non-substitutable scopes; execute approved ordered/hold/stop sequences, coordinate shared equipment; North blocks unready-interlock closing; send timestamped Bay Status Digest to Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing). Breaker Control Unit requires authorization/interlocks/permitted modes; local authority prevails. North Protection Panel contains feeder protection; Transformer Protection Panel independently protects transformer, indicates operations locally. Feeder Protection Relay (Tandem) independently protects with approved settings; produces Relay Diagnostic Note. Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur) investigates; revisioned settings require independent approval, compatibility/installation/functional checks; discrepancies block release.
Glasswing produces Alarm Acknowledgement Slip, retains cleared alarm/event history, separates archives/current quality; communications recovery requires currency verification. Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin) sends Clock Drift Snapshot to Sequence Event Archive (Orchard); distributes timing reference; loss invokes holdover; synchronized/degraded/unavailable quality cannot validate protection/measurement. Orchard preserves ordered evidence, timestamps/uncertainty/corrections/history; requires auditable access, retention/holds, protected backups, recovery checks and faithful exports/restoration. Station DC System powers protection/automation; produces Battery Load Test Record. Engineering Workstation controls revisions/history; produces Settings Review Receipt; authorized bounded review never substitutes immediate assessment. Maintenance Remote Terminal enables authorized maintenance. Station Gateway produces Protocol Retry Summary; brokers authorized control-room/bay traffic using configured mappings/addressing/access controls; supervisory/bay/protection layers remain separate on loss.
Substation Supervisor resolves authorization/escalation. Substation Field Crew (Cinder) verifies identity/local safety; sends Breaker Inspection Tag; discrepancies hold/escalate. Switching Desk Coordinator (Keystone) produces Isolation Boundary Card; confirms handback before engineering review. Control Room Operator reviews alarm/device/sequence, feeder/protection/DC status before acknowledging; records response/outstanding actions on slip; clearing proves no correction; breaker discrepancies remain abnormal pending understanding; produces Clearance Handoff Memo for unresolved handoff; verifies alarm/equipment/evidence consistency after handback before closure.

New part:
S173: It rejects malformed, stale, or unauthorized requests and records each rejection with enough context for operations review.
S174: Station Supervisory Control System presents available controls and indications to authorized operating personnel.
S175: Control Room Operator issues state-changing requests only through approved operating procedures and the configured supervisory interface.
S176: Bay Automation Controller validates each received request against local mode, interlocks, command authority, and equipment availability before issuing bay-level outputs.
S177: Breaker Control Unit applies accepted output commands at the breaker interface and returns the resulting position and circuit-health indications.
S178: Bay Automation Controller compares returned indications with the requested state and identifies incomplete or contradictory operation.
S179: Bay Automation Controller uses the inspection tag to associate the applicable equipment context with an authorized record.
S180: Station Gateway carries updated indications through the station interface using configured quality and timestamp attributes.
S181: Station Supervisory Control System displays indication quality and stale-data status so operators can distinguish a current value from a retained value.
S182: Sequence Event Archive retains time-tagged changes and control outcomes for event reconstruction and operational review.
S183: Satellite Time Receiver supplies the station time reference used to align event timestamps, subject to configured quality checks.
S184: Bay Automation Controller monitors communication health and places affected points in a defined degraded state when updates exceed configured age limits.
S185: Station Gateway reports link condition and protocol errors without converting a communication failure into an equipment-state change.
S186: Tandem evaluates electrical quantities against approved settings and issues protective trip outputs without relying on supervisory communications.
S187: North Protection Panel applies its assigned zone logic and maintains trip paths independently of supervisory network availability.
S188: Transformer Protection Panel applies its assigned protective logic and reports abnormal protection conditions through its configured interface.
S189: North Bay Controller maintains local bay control within the approved operating mode when supervisory communications are interrupted.
S190: South Bay Controller reports local mode and control availability through its configured bay interface.
S191: Engineering Workstation supports approved configuration review and does not serve as a routine source of operating commands.
S192: Maintenance Remote Terminal access is restricted to authorized maintenance sessions and is not used to bypass local interlocks.
S193: Station DC System supports control and protection functions through monitored station supply circuits, and supply loss is indicated as an abnormal station condition.
S194: Protection Relay Engineer reviews protection event records and verifies that approved settings remain consistent with coordination requirements.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
